payload.title: Ceratocaudia
payload.wikitext:
{{Short description|Genus of sauropod dinosaur}} {{Automatic taxobox | fossil_range =
[[Jurassic]], ~{{Fossilrange|earliest=Pliensbachian|Bajocian|Bajocian|?[[Pliensbachian]] to [[Bajocian]]}} | image = Ceratocaudia antiqua (skeletal reconstruction).png | image_caption = Silhouette with known material of ''C. antiqua'' indicated | taxon = Ceratocaudia | authority = Abhishek et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | type_species = {{extinct}}'''''Ceratocaudia antiqua''''' | type_species_authority = Abhishek et al., 2026 }} '''''Ceratocaudia''''' ({{lit|horned tail}}) is a genus of [[macronaria]]n [[sauropod]] dinosaur from the [[Jurassic]] [[Kaladongar Formation]] of [[Gujarat]], India. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Ceratocaudia antiqua''''', known from a partial skeleton.{{Cite journal |last1=Abhishek |first1=N. |last2=Bhosale |first2=S. |last3=Rakshit |first3=N. |last4=Dasgupta |first4=S. |year=2026 |title=A new diminutive Jurassic neosauropod from the Kaladongar Formation (Khadir Uplift) of the Kachchh Basin, western India |journal=Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology |article-number=e2677749 |doi=10.1080/02724634.2026.2677749 }} == Discovery and naming == The ''Ceratocaudia antiqua'' [[holotype]] specimen was collected from the low-energy estuarine sediments of the Khadir Uplift of [[Kaladongar Formation]] in [[Kutch district]] of Gujarat, India. It consists a [[cervical vertebra|cervical]] (neck) and several [[caudal vertebra|caudal]] (tail) [[vertebrae]], an isolated [[chevron (anatomy)|chevron]], and elements of the [[appendicular skeleton]] including an [[interclavicle]], an [[ulna]] (forearm bone), [[metacarpal]]s (finger bones), [[femora]] (thighbones), [[tibiae]], [[fibulae]] (lower leg bones), and a [[metatarsal]] (toe bone). They are housed in the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]] in [[Mumbai]], India, where they are permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] under as IITBR3–IITBR59. In 2026, Abhishek Natarajan and colleagues [[Species description|described]] the remains as belonging to a new genus and species of sauropod dinosaur. The [[generic name (biology)|generic name]], ''Ceratocaudia'', comes from the [[Ancient Greek]] word [[wikt:κέρας|κέρας]], meaning {{gloss|horn}}, and the [[Latin]] word [[wikt:cauda#Latin|cauda]], meaning {{gloss|tail}}, after the horn-like crest on the anterior caudal neural spine. The [[specific name]], ''antiqua'', is a Latin word meaning {{gloss|ancient}}. == Description == [[File:Ceratocaudia antiqua.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]] The ''Ceratocaudia'' holotype is estimated to belong to an animal about {{convert|7|m|ft}} long, making it one of the smallest known macronarians. There is a possibility that it represents a dwarf taxon. Based on [[histological]] analysis and the presence of a non-traumatic [[pathology]], the holotype appears to have been a [[senescence|senescent]] (old) individual. A reconstructed muscle model of the tail suggests it could have been used to deter predators. == Classification == To determine the relationships of ''Ceratocaudia'', Abhishek et al. (2026) scored it in the [[phylogenetic analysis|phylogenetic]] matrices of Mannion & Moore (2025){{Cite journal |last1=Mannion |first1=Philip D. |last2=Moore |first2=Andrew J. |date=2025-10-10 |title=Critical reappraisal of a putative dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of Gondwana and a revised view of diplodocoid evolutionary relationships and biogeography |journal=[[Journal of Systematic Palaeontology]] |language=en |volume=23 |issue=1 |doi=10.1080/14772019.2025.2550760 |issn=1477-2019|doi-access=free }} and Pérez Moreno et al. (2023).{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1016/j.cretres.2022.105389| issn = 0195-6671| article-number = 105389| last1 = Pérez Moreno| first1 = Agustín| last2 = Otero| first2 = Alejandro| last3 = Carballido| first3 = José L.| last4 = Salgado| first4 = Leonardo| last5 = Calvo| first5 = Jorge O.| title = The appendicular skeleton of Rinconsaurus caudamirus (Sauropoda: Titanosauria) from the Upper Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina| journal = Cretaceous Research| date = 2022-10-07| volume = 142| bibcode = 2023CrRes.14205389P| s2cid = 252799392}} Both analyses placed ''Ceratocaudia'' within the [[Macronaria]], outside the [[Titanosauriformes]], making it one of the oldest such sauropods and adding to the evidence of a global pre-Bajocian distribution of macronarians. The reduced strict consensus results of the Mannion & Moore (2025) dataset, pruning 21 taxa, is shown in the [[cladogram]] below: {{clade |label1=[[Macronaria]] |1={{clade |1={{clade |1={{clade |1={{clade |1=''[[Lourinhasaurus]]'' |2=''[[Camarasaurus]]'' }} |2={{clade |1=''[[Tehuelchesaurus]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Haestasaurus]]'' |2=''[[Janenschia]]'' }} }} }} |2={{clade |1={{clade |1=''[[Mierasaurus]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Moabosaurus]]'' |2=''[[Tendaguria]]'' }} }} |2={{clade |1=''[[Zby]]'' |2=''[[Turiasaurus]]'' |3=''[[Losillasaurus]]'' }} }} }} |2={{clade sequential |1=''[[Aragosaurus]]'' |2='''''Ceratocaudia''''' |3=''[[Galveosaurus]]'' |4=[[Titanosauriformes]] }} }} }} == Paleoecology == The sediments in which ''Ceratocaudia'' was found also consist of abundant [[petrified wood]] and [[Bivalvia|bivalves]] like ''[[Protocardia]]'' and ''[[Indocorbula]]'' that lived in brackish waters. The Khadir Uplift, of a different horizon but of the same age, has yielded a large fragmentary [[Sauropoda|sauropod]] which is estimated to be 20 metres long, as well as the [[hybodont]] shark ''[[Strophodus magnus]]''. The presence of a large contemporary sauropod suggests niche partitioning between it and ''Ceratocaudia'', though it is unknown what ecological role they had in their environment, as both lack cranial material. == References == {{Reflist}} {{Sauropodomorpha|M.}} {{Portal bar|Dinosaurs|India}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q140589467}} [[Category:Macronaria]] [[Category:Dinosaur genera]] [[Category:Pliensbachian dinosaurs]] [[Category:Toarcian dinosaurs]] [[Category:Aalenian dinosaurs]] [[Category:Bajocian dinosaurs]] [[Category:Dinosaurs of India]] [[Category:Fossil taxa described in 2026]]
